goal: select_next_task and WorkGraph.ready_set offer ready items highest-priority-first (ties in walk order) and exclude items whose required_capabilities are not a subset of the worker's advertised capability set.

relevant: .flywheel/specs/00049-distributed-scheduling-metadata.md -- acceptance criteria #4, #5, #6, #7 and decisions D-1, D-2 this task satisfies

packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_workflow.py -- select_next_task (~line 284): order eligible candidates by descending priority (stable, walk-order tie-break) and apply the capability filter
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_work_graph.py -- WorkGraph.ready_set (~line 257): same priority ordering and capability filter over the runnable set

packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_policy.py -- WorkPolicy and the [execution] table (execution_mode ~line 323): add the per-worker capability set config (default empty), threaded into selection
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/tests/test_workflow.py -- keep this suite green; it pins select_next_task's selection/ordering
constraints: Priority is a stable descending sort over the current candidate sequence: among equal-priority items, existing enumeration/walk order is preserved. Default priority 0 means an all-default set sorts to its original walk order -- today's first-eligible behavior exactly.

Capability filter: an item is selectable/runnable by a worker iff its required_capabilities is a subset of the worker's advertised capability set. An item with empty required_capabilities is selectable by any worker, including a worker with an empty capability set.

The worker's capability set is an explicit per-worker configuration value (its home is the [execution] table), defaulting to empty. Thread it into selection so the default (empty) preserves current signatures' behavior and no caller is forced to pass it.
Both behaviors apply in both execution modes (local and distributed).
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do NOT reuse or rename [sandbox.capabilities] / SandboxCapabilities -- that is the agent tool/skill/MCP surface, a different concept (D-2).
Do NOT touch the claim store -- conflict-key exclusion and the liveness sweep are later tasks.
Do NOT add WorkItem fields or change persistence -- the prerequisite task owns those.
Do NOT modify files under tests/; do not weaken or delete existing selection assertions.
edge_cases: Priorities [1, 9, 5] in walk order must be offered 9, 5, 1; priorities [3, 3, 3] must preserve walk order -- a sort that reorders equal-priority items (e.g. by id) must fail.
An empty-capability worker must still be offered every existing (zero-requirement) item; adding one item requiring {"gpu"} must withhold that item alone while the rest are unaffected.
A worker with capability set {"gpu"} must be offered an item requiring {} and one requiring {"gpu"} but not one requiring {"gpu","cuda"}.
